**Answer**

A parser reads text in a fixed format and turns it into a structured form a program can use.

**Why**

Text alone is just characters. A program needs to know what each part means. A parser checks that the text follows the rules of its language. It groups characters into meaningful pieces like words, numbers, or symbols. It then builds a tree or list that shows how those pieces relate. Compilers use parsers to turn source code into something a computer can run. Browsers use parsers to turn HTML into a page structure. JSON parsers turn JSON strings into objects your code can read.
